required_floor_classes.lane_definition: A Social Security scenario cannot pass if eligible old-age, survivor, or disability beneficiaries lose coverage, claim access, timely benefit access, or language/disability access without explicit remediation.
A Social Security scenario cannot pass if lower cost or higher receipts are achieved by degrading payment accuracy, claims processing quality, disability determination quality, or appeal rights.

A Social Security scenario cannot pass if it shifts benefit loss, tax burden, claiming burden, or longevity risk onto lower-income, disabled, survivor, older, or high-risk cohorts without reviewed distributional evidence.
A Social Security scenario cannot pass if it reduces replacement adequacy, old-age poverty protection, disability protection, survivor protection, or trust-fund resilience below reviewed floors.

A Social Security scenario cannot pass without explicit OASDI trust-fund accounting, annual demographic path, legal authority, implementation cost, administration burden, behavior model, incidence model, and transition feasibility.

social_security_specific_floor_definitio.definition: Benefit replacement rates require sourced cohort, earnings-history, age, and claiming-year values before any scenario can pass.
Old-age poverty and near-poverty protection require sourced baseline, policy, and stress values before any lower-cost scenario can pass.
Disability and survivor benefit continuity, adequacy, access, determination quality, and appeal-right effects require explicit review.
OASI, DI, and combined OASDI accounting must remain explicit; trust-fund transfers or reallocations cannot be implicit.
Implementation timing, SSA workload, notices, systems, appeals, enforcement, compliance, and taxpayer burden require explicit sourced values.

public_warning_phrases: This Social Security floor packet defines required floor concepts, but it does not set threshold values or pass/fail findings.
OASDI trust-fund accounting remains separate; transfers or reallocations must be explicit and cannot be inferred.

No lower-cost Social Security scenario is admissible until replacement adequacy, old-age poverty, disability/survivor protection, access, equity, and delivery-feasibility floors are thresholded, sourced, reviewed, and passed.
No target cost, federal effect, gross savings, net savings, assigned-base rate, solver input, department-cut instruction, technology-savings claim, or balanced-budget claim is populated.
No FOIA request, records request, form, email, phone call, or agency/person contact was submitted.

This record is not outcome-floor passage, not a demographic score, not a trust-fund solvency score, not a target-cost selection, not solver input, not a solver run, not a rate calculation, not a public rate card, not a tax proposal, not a savings estimate, not a waste finding, not a fraud finding, not a department-cut instruction, not a technology-savings claim, and not a balanced-budget claim.
